statements.text: The first H. salicifolia mitochondrial genome measured 475,105 bp, had 44.80% GC content and contained 74 genes, 37 of them protein-coding.
statements.evidence: The 475,105 bp genome has a 44.80% GC content and an overall AT bias, comprising 74 genes (37 protein-coding, 31 tRNA, three rRNA, and three pseudogenes).
statements.note: Length, GC content and the gene inventory are all given in the abstract.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: RNA editing was found at 415 sites, most of which replace a hydrophilic amino acid with a hydrophobic one.
statements.evidence: RNA editing analysis revealed 415 sites that mostly convert hydrophilic to hydrophobic amino acids
statements.note: The site count and the predominant direction of the amino acid change are stated.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The SSRs identified separate Himalayan H. salicifolia populations growing at different altitudes.
statements.evidence: We identified extensive repetitive elements, including 188 SSRs, 20 tandem repeats, and 455 dispersed repeats, and explored their potential roles in genome evolution.
statements.note: The repeats are catalogued and discussed for genome evolution, but no population or altitudinal sampling is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Extensive gene transfer was detected between the mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes, and most genes were under purifying selection.
statements.evidence: In addition, extensive gene transfer was detected between the mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes. Ka/Ks and nucleotide diversity analyses indicate that most genes are under purifying selection, with some possibly undergoing positive selection.
statements.note: Both the organelle gene transfer and the predominance of purifying selection are reported.
